scholarships.title: MOPGA 2027: Visiting Fellowship Program for Early Career Researchers
scholarships.official_source: Campus France, funded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (MEAE) in partnership with the Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space (MESRE)

existing.description: MOPGA is a French Government visiting fellowship that pays a monthly allowance to early-career foreign researchers to carry out a 12-month research project in a French host laboratory on climate and environmental themes. Each fellowship covers a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance, and health, civil liability and repatriation coverage. Host laboratories receive no funding under the programme; the money is intended solely to cover the invited researcher's living expenses, and international travel costs are not covered.
eligibility: Hold a doctoral degree awarded less than five years before the application deadline, i.e. have defended your PhD thesis between December 2021 and December 2026 inclusive
Be exclusively of foreign nationality (all nationalities are eligible except French nationality)
Apply for the purpose of undertaking international mobility to France
Not be residing and professionally active in France at the time of application
Not have previously received a MOPGA fellowship
existing.eligibility_summary: Foreign researchers whose PhD was defended between December 2021 and December 2026 inclusive, applying from outside France for a research stay in France.
benefits: Status of French Government Scholarship holder (BGF)
Fellowship paid directly by Campus France
Research stay agreement signed between the French host institution and the researcher
coverage: Health coverage: health insurance, civil liability insurance and repatriation assistance, followed by supplementary health insurance once the fellow has been registered with the French social security system
requirements: Applications must be submitted online through the Campus France SMApply platform; applications sent by email will not be considered
A research stay agreement must be signed between the host institution in France and the researcher
Host laboratories undertake to provide an appropriate scientific environment for the research stay, but do not receive any funding under the programme

This French Government fellowship cannot be combined with a French employment contract, such as a research contract or postdoctoral contract, or with any other individual funding awarded by a French government entity
Research project must fall within one of the five MOPGA research areas
documents: CV including a list of publications (4 pages max.)
Doctoral degree certificate (or official proof of degree)
CV of the scientific supervisor at the host laboratory (2 pages max.)

Letter of support from the scientific supervisor, co-signed by the laboratory director or accompanied by a letter of commitment from the laboratory director, confirming that the scientific environment and resources required will be made available and that the project is consistent with the laboratory's objectives
Copy of passport or national identity document
application_method: Agree the research project with a host laboratory in France and obtain the host director's commitment

Prepare the research project description: project title, 6 keywords, summary, background and motivation, scientific objectives, methodology and timeline, relevance to MOPGA, and international collaboration or expected impact
Collect the required documents, including supervisor CV and the co-signed support letter
Submit the application online via https://campusfrance.smapply.io/prog/mopga_2027/ before 15 December 2026
existing.selection_notes: Selection takes place in two stages: scientific experts appointed by the French Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space in the relevant fields assess the applications received, then a scientific committee makes the final selection. Innovative approaches involving advanced technologies within the eligible research areas are given particular consideration during the selection process.
existing.best_fit: Researchers who defended a PhD between December 2021 and December 2026, hold a nationality other than French, are not resident and professionally active in France, and have already lined up a French host laboratory willing to sign a research stay agreement.
existing.notes: The fellowship is not renewable and lasts exactly 12 months. International travel costs to France are not covered by the programme; the host laboratory may be able to help but is not funded to do so. The award cannot be combined with a French employment contract (research contract or postdoctoral contract) or any other individual funding from a French government entity. A PhD defended after December 2026 is not eligible. If the doctoral degree certificate has not yet been issued, an official certificate confirming the defence, proof of thesis submission, or another official institutional document is accepted. For researchers who obtained their PhD more than five years ago, the eligibility window may be extended by 18 months per child, or by the actual duration of maternity leave, on submission of supporting documents noted in the application file. Only projects with a genuine integrated 'One Health' approach qualify under the human, animal and environmental health theme; projects focused solely on medicine or human health are not eligible.
existing.application_period: Applications open 15 September 2026 and close 15 December 2026. Results are notified May-June 2027, and successful applicants arrive in France between September and December 2027.

scholarships.title: PhD Position F/M Spatio-temporal analysis of remote sensing data at large scales (Inria offer 2026-10352)
scholarships.official_source: Inria (Centre Inria d'Universite Cote d'Azur, TITANE team)

existing.description: Inria, the French national institute for research in digital science and technology, recruits PhD students as fixed-term salaried employment contracts rather than as scholarship holders. This post is a 3-year doctoral contract at the Centre Inria d'Universite Cote d'Azur (team TITANE, Sophia Antipolis) with a published gross monthly salary of EUR 2,300, starting 1 December 2026. The work sits inside the JUNN Digital Twin of France and its Territories project, on detecting and analysing 3D change from airborne LidarHD and satellite Digital Surface Model data at national scale.
eligibility: Level of qualifications required: Graduate degree or equivalent
Strong background in 3D geometry, computer vision and machine learning
Able to program in C/C++ and Python
existing.eligibility_summary: Candidates need a graduate degree or equivalent, a strong background in 3D geometry, computer vision and machine learning, C/C++ and Python programming skills, and fluent English.
benefits: All Inria positions are accessible to people with disabilities under the institute's diversity policy
coverage: Gross salary of EUR 2,300 per month under a fixed-term contract
Partial reimbursement of public transport costs
Leave: 7 weeks of annual leave plus 10 extra days off due to RTT, with possibility of exceptional leave
Possibility of teleworking and flexible organisation of working hours
Professional equipment available (videoconferencing, loan of computer equipment)
Access to vocational training and to social, cultural and sports events and activities
Contribution to mutual insurance (subject to conditions)
requirements: Applications must be submitted online on the Inria website; collecting applications through other channels is not guaranteed
An e-mail address must be entered in order to save the application to Inria

The position is likely to be situated in a restricted area (ZRR) under Decree No. 2011-1425 on the protection of national scientific and technical potential (PPST); authorisation to enter is granted by the director of the unit following a favourable Ministerial decision as defined in the decree of 3 July 2012
Processing of applications sent through channels other than the Inria website is not guaranteed
existing.english_requirement: Fluent in English (published in the Skills section of the official posting: 'be fluent in English')
application_method: Read the full topic description published by the TITANE team and the JUNN project pages linked from the posting
Create an account or sign in on the Inria website so the application can be saved
Complete and submit the application through the 'Apply for this position' form on the Inria posting
Submit before the published deadline of 30 November 2026
existing.selection_notes: Inria recruits through its own online application system; the posting does not publish a selection method, timetable or assessment criteria beyond the stated skill profile and the accessibility commitment for people with disabilities.
existing.best_fit: Master's-level graduate with a strong background in 3D geometry, computer vision and machine learning, able to program in C/C++ and Python and fluent in English, who wants to work on 3D urban reconstruction and change detection within a French national research institute.
existing.notes: This is a fixed-term paid employment contract, not a scholarship: the applicant is hired by Inria and is subject to the labour code, social security and the institute's HR rules. The published EUR 2,300 is a gross monthly salary, not a total cost-of-living grant, so it must not be read as full funding of tuition, housing and living expenses. Crucially, this post is likely to be located in a restricted area (ZRR): authorisation to enter requires a favourable Ministerial decision, and an unfavourable decision in respect of a position situated in a ZRR results in the cancellation of the appointment. The posting does not state the date on which the position was posted, so the effective remaining time to apply should be checked on the live Inria posting.
existing.application_period: Applications are accepted online on the Inria website until 30 November 2026. The contract starts on 1 December 2026 and runs for 3 years.
